title: drogna monitor configuration
description: Configuration for C-11, the divergence monitor. Every number that decides whether the harness spends a model run is here, because over-sensitivity is the failure this component owns and a threshold buried in source is a threshold nobody tunes. The common sections are referenced from config.common.schema.json rather than restated, and unknown keys are rejected so that a typo is a startup failure rather than a silent default.

window.title: The rolling window
window.description: Bounded in both simulation-time span and sample count, so it cannot grow with the length of the scenario. Eviction is by simulation time; the count bound is what holds the memory footprint at a high clock rate.

span_seconds.description: How far back the window reaches, in seconds of simulation time.

maximum_samples.description: Hard bound on samples held. The oldest is evicted when it is reached.

maximum_pending.description: Bound on observations accepted but not yet paired into a scoreable sample. Beyond it the oldest are shed and counted, because falling behind unboundedly at a high clock rate is worse than a reported drop.

residual.title: The residual and its threshold
residual.description: The residual is defined on sound speed, derived from the observed temperature, salinity and pressure by the single implementation in harness_core (ADR-0005). There is no threshold on temperature here, and there is not meant to be.

threshold_m_per_s.description: Residual magnitude above which a sample counts towards persistence, in metres per second. Of the order of 1.5 to 2 m/s, which is roughly half a degree Celsius at the scenario's nominal conditions.

persistence.title: What makes a divergence rather than a spike
persistence.description: Either rule may be satisfied. Both counts are at least two, because a single sample above threshold is an outlier and raising a run for it is the failure this component owns.

neighbourhood_radius_m.description: Radius within which samples count as neighbours, in metres. A radius and not a spatial index: indexing belongs to the planner, and coupling the monitor to it would buy nothing.

spatial_sample_count.description: Distinct samples above threshold inside one neighbourhood that satisfy the spatial rule.

temporal_sample_count.description: Consecutive samples above threshold that satisfy the temporal rule.

temporal_span_seconds.description: Simulation-time span those consecutive samples must cover, in seconds. Without it a burst arriving in one instant would satisfy a rule about persistence over time.

warmup.title: Starting and restarting
warmup.description: On start or restart the monitor has no window. It either observes a span of simulation time or issues exactly one catch-up query against the observation store, and publishes no divergence until that completes.

mode.description: span: wait out the declared simulation-time span. catchup: one query to the observation store, and no further query for the life of the process.

span_seconds.description: The warm-up span in seconds of simulation time, and in catchup mode the span the single query covers.

catchup_sample_limit.description: Bound on the rows the single catch-up query returns, so a restart cannot pull the store into memory.

coverage.title: Reading the current forecast
coverage.description: The monitor samples the forecast through the coverage read port, not through the query layer: it sits inside the boundary, and routing an internal consumer out through the external read path and back would claim a seam that is not there.

current_pointer.description: Name of the text file in the root holding one run identifier on one line (ADR-0011). Two identifiers means two runs claim to be current, and the reader reports no current forecast rather than choosing one.

runs_dirname.description: Name of the directory under the root holding the run directories. The pointer names a run, not a path, so the reader needs this to find it.

forecast_file.description: Name of the forecast field inside a run's directory.
